_doc.what: Per-asset parameters for rig_character.py (Stage 3b of the Siegebound art pipeline — the SKELETAL rig/anim tooling, TASK-160). Sibling of pipeline_manifest.json (the static TRELLIS.2 pipeline). Law: CONVENTIONS.md 'Skeletal rig & animation workstream (M7)'.
_doc.why_separate_manifest: The mesh pipeline (pipeline_manifest.json) and the rig pipeline are COMPLEMENTARY but disjoint stages (SM_<CardID> backs the ghost + fallback; SK_<CardID> is the animated runtime). Keeping rig params here avoids perturbing the carefully-authored mesh manifest and keeps the rig tooling self-contained.
_doc.merging: 'defaults' apply to every asset; per-asset keys override (dict values merge one level deep) — identical to pipeline_manifest.json.
_doc.skeleton: The SHARED humanoid skeleton is 'SiegeBiped' (-> UE 'SKEL_SiegeBiped'). Bone NAMES + hierarchy are the retarget contract: every humanoid unit rigged on 'SiegeBiped' gets identical bone names so UE can share/retarget one skeleton + author locomotion once. Bone POSITIONS are computed per-asset in rig_character.py from the MEASURED game-ready mesh (adaptive fit) x the normalized 'proportions' below, so the same skeleton spec fits a 149-tall militiaman and a 208-tall cavalry rider. Non-humanoid assets (e.g. Ogre) may set skeleton:'bespoke' to get their own auto-skeleton later.
_doc.proportions: Normalized humanoid anchors. *_z are fractions of measured mesh HEIGHT (0=feet, 1=head-top). *_x_frac multiply the MEASURED half-width at that region (shoulder_half / hip_half) so limb roots sit inside the silhouette. foot_forward_frac is a fraction of height (foot points -Y = front). A-pose arms (nearly straight down) maximize skin quality for TRELLIS meshes whose arms rest at the sides.
_doc.skinning: 'auto_then_envelope' = try Blender bone-heat automatic weights first; if it errors or leaves > unweighted_fallback_fraction of verts empty, fall back to deterministic segment-distance envelope weighting (never fails, generalizes to the batch). Recorded in rig_report.json.
_doc.anims: Frame LENGTHS at 'fps'. Required actions Idle/Walk/Attack/Death (CONVENTIONS). 'weapon_side' picks which arm drives Attack (r bones sit at -X = the character's right, matching the Footman spear at -X). 'attack_style' selects the Attack pose set in rig_character.py (thrust|swing|overhead|cast|mine).
_doc.outputs: rig_character.py writes the rigged mesh FBX to Content/RawAssets/Characters/<CardID>.fbx and one anim FBX per action to Content/RawAssets/Characters/Anims/<CardID>_<Action>.fbx (raw-asset rule). Previews (turntable + per-anim mp4 + bind stills + contact sheets) + rig_report.json go to Cache/<CardID>/rig/. The AM_<CardID>_Attack MONTAGE is authored in-editor at TASK-162 from A_<CardID>_Attack (a montage wraps a sequence — not a Blender export).

SiegeBiped._desc: 21-bone humanoid: root(non-deform) + pelvis + spine_01/02/03 + neck_01 + head + [clavicle/upperarm/lowerarm/hand]_l|r + [thigh/calf/foot]_l|r. UE-mannequin-style names for future Manny retarget potential. _l bones sit at +X (character's LEFT), _r at -X (character's RIGHT — the -X weapon side).

Footman._note: Pilot rig spike (TASK-160). Simplest humanoid, already textured (SM_Footman, 15000 tris, [TeamRegion, FootmanPBR], UVMap, feet-center ~180 UE). Spear at -X per pipeline_manifest.json => weapon_side 'r' + 'thrust'. Proves the shared SiegeBiped humanoid rig for the batch (TASK-163/164).

Ogre._note: TASK-242 evening batch. GDD S4/S3.8: Unit, 500 HP, dmg 35, range 120, Siege tank (ignores units, targets buildings then castle). ROSTER'S TALLEST (Z 290 UE = 2.90 m; X 226.72 includes the stone-maul overhang). Wizard._note: TASK-302 W-UNIT-1. CONVENTIONS 'Wizard unit — AoE fireball caster': ranged Standard-profile fireball caster, robed humanoid (the Cleric robed-caster precedent). Rigged on the SHARED SiegeBiped (Footman_Rig root) like every humanoid; the adaptive height/half-width fit absorbs the outstretched fireball arm + held staff (TASK-301: bounds [129.88,99.25,181.94] UE, Z height-fit to 182 = 1.82 m; footprint deeper than a stock humanoid per the Cavalry/Ogre weapon-overhang note). 'cast' (script else-branch = raise-arm-then-drive-forward) reads as a spellcast/HURL, deliberately NOT 'thrust' (the Archer/Longbowman bow-draw read the spec bars). weapon_side 'r' drives the STAFF arm (staff in the right hand; fireball cradled in the left palm per TASK-301) up-and-forward = iconic staff-cast silhouette at RTS camera. FLAG (Cleric/Archer flag class): a true two-hand fireball-hurl (left-hand throw) or a Meshy cast clip is a tuning follow-up, not required now. Two-slot [TeamRegion, WizardPBR]+UVMap.
